old: so worthy in his look of reverence
new: so worthy of reverence in his look
why: degno di tanta reverenza in vista: worthy of reverence in appearance, not a reverent look. Longfellow agrees.

old: brought back the delight to my eyes
new: brought delight back to my eyes
why: a li occhi miei ricominciò diletto; the stray article trips the line.

old: every stain that hell has left on it
new: every stain that clings to it
why: sì ch'ogne sucidume quindi stinghe: 'that hell has left' is an added gloss.

old:
"In exitu Israel de Aegypto" —
When Israel went out of Egypt — all of them
sang it together, in one voice, to the end,
new:
"In exitu Israel de Aegypto,"
they all sang together, in one voice,
with everything that psalm sets down thereafter.
why: Policy T (tercet realignment, Canto II): Dante 46-48 leaves the psalm in Latin; the English gloss line is removed and the tercet closes on 'scripto'.

old:
with everything that psalm sets down thereafter.
Then he traced the holy cross above them,
and they flung themselves, every one, onto the strand,
new:
Then he traced the holy cross above them,
and they flung themselves, every one, onto the strand,
and he was gone, as swiftly as he had come.
why: Policy T (tercet realignment, Canto II): back on Dante 49-51 (Poi fece il segno ... veloce); line moved up from seg-0018.

old:
and he was gone, as swiftly as he had come.
The crowd left standing there seemed strangers
to the place, looking all around them,
new:
The crowd left standing there seemed strangers
to the place, looking all around them,
like someone testing out new things.
why: Policy T (tercet realignment, Canto II): back on Dante 52-54 (La turba ... assaggia); line moved up from seg-0019.

old:
like someone testing out new things.
On every side the day was breaking now —
the sun, with his bright shafts, had chased
new:
On every side the day was breaking now —
the sun, with his bright shafts, had chased
the Capricorn down out of the high middle sky —
why: Policy T (tercet realignment, Canto II): back on Dante 55-57 (Da tutte parti ... Capricorno); line moved up from seg-0020.

old:
the Capricorn down out of the high middle sky —
when the new people lifted their faces toward us
and said: "If you know it, show us the way
new:
when the new people lifted their faces toward us
and said: "If you know it, show us the way
to go up the mountain."
why: Policy T (tercet realignment, Canto II): back on Dante 58-60, ending on 'gire al monte'.

old:
to go up the mountain." And Virgil answered:
"You think, perhaps, that we know this place,
but we are strangers here, the same as you.
why: Policy T (tercet realignment, Canto II): back on Dante 61-63 (E Virgilio rispuose: 'Voi credete / forse che siamo esperti d'esto loco; / ma noi siam peregrin come voi siete'); wording otherwise kept.

old: like people going who don't know where; nor was our own leaving
new:
like people going who don't know where;
nor was our own leaving
why: Policy C (closing line): Dante 133 'né la nostra partita fu men tosta' is the canto's closing line; the edition has no 45th segment, so it is restored as its own line at the end of seg-0044.

old: how were so many years taken from you?
new: how was so much time taken from you?
why: Ma a te com' era tanta ora tolta?: 'so much time', the delay; 'years' is added.

old:
fanning the air with feathers that never fall,
that do not molt away
new:
fanning the air with his eternal feathers
that do not molt away
why: trattando l'aere con l'etterne penne: 'never fall' and 'do not molt' said the same thing twice.

old: so all those lucky spirits
new: so all those fortunate spirits
why: anime fortunate; 'lucky' is too casual.

old:
That people was still as far from us —
a thousand of our steps, I'd say —
as a good arm could throw a stone,
new:
Even after we had gone a thousand steps,
that people was still as far from us
as a good arm could throw a stone,
why: Ancora era quel popol di lontano, / i' dico dopo i nostri mille passi, / quanto un buon gittator trarria con mano: the thousand steps are what they had walked; the distance is still a stone's throw.

old: Be content with the because, humankind.
new: Be content, humankind, with knowing that it is.
why: State contenti, umana gente, al quia: the scholastic quia is the bare fact, set against the why; 'the because' says the opposite.

old: and you have watched men long without end —
new: and you have seen men long for it in vain —
why: e disïar vedeste sanza frutto: desire 'without fruit', not without end.

old: the leader of that lucky flock
new: the leader of that fortunate flock
why: mandra fortunata; same word as Canto II, same fix.

old: Giovanna, no one — no one cares for me;
new: Neither Giovanna nor anyone else cares for me;
why: Giovanna o altri non ha di me cura: Giovanna (his widow) is the subject, not someone addressed. Longfellow: 'Giovanna, nor none other cares for me'.

old: as long as can't doesn't cut off will.
new: so long as "I cannot" does not cut off "I will."
why: pur che 'l voler nonpossa non ricida: the two words are quoted nouns; bare they read as verbs.

old:
Many carry justice in their hearts, but the shot
comes slow, so it won't leave the bow unconsidered;
new:
Many hold justice in their hearts, but loose it slowly,
so it won't leave the bow without thought;
why: Molti han giustizia in cuore, e tardi scocca / per non venir sanza consiglio a l'arco: the archery image untangled.

old:
Pedro, who sings with him —
for whom Provence and Apulia already grieve.
new:
Pedro, who sings with him;
and so Provence and Apulia grieve already.
why: onde Puglia e Proenza già si dole: they grieve because of the large-nosed Charles's heir, not for Pedro.

old: Before the little sun goes down to its nest
new: Before what little sun is left goes to its nest
why: Prima che 'l poco sole omai s'annidi: what little sun remains.

old: "See you wash these wounds
new: "Be sure you wash these wounds
why: Fa che lavi ... queste piaghe; 'See you' first reads as a farewell.

old: was glowing white at the eastern rail,
new: was glowing white on the balcony of the east,
why: al balco d'orïente; 'rail' reads as a fence.

old: bars of heavy, ringing metal —
new: which are of heavy, ringing metal —
why: li spigoli ... che di metallo son sonanti e forti: the pivots are the metal; 'bars' adds an object.

old:
"Lord, give me justice
for my dead son.
new:
"Lord, avenge me
for my dead son.
why: Segnor, fammi vendetta: she asks for vengeance; Trajan's 'justice' answer (seg-0031) depends on the difference.

old: made this speech you could see —
new: made this visible speech —
why: visibile parlare: the known phrase restored.

old: the peace that broke Heaven's long embargo,
new: the peace that opened Heaven after its long ban,
why: ch'aperse il ciel del suo lungo divieto; 'embargo' is a trade-policy word.

old: if you let your own slide?"
new: if you forget your own?"
why: se la tua metti in oblio: put out of mind; 'let slide' is too casual.

old: why men dread an office not given them to hold.
new: for which men dread an office not given them to hold.
why: per che si teme officio non commesso: the line hangs on the ark (Uzzah); 'why' reads as a stray fragment.

old: unless a coarse age follows and dims the rest.
new: unless a cruder age comes after it.
why: se non è giunta da l'etati grosse: 'and dims the rest' is added and changes the sense.

old: to beg — to tremble in every vein.
new: to tremble in every vein.
why: si condusse a tremar per ogne vena: 'to beg' is a gloss; the begging is implied by the Campo scene.

old:
made the fatal necklace cost his mother
so dearly for what she wore.
new:
made his mother pay so dearly
for the ill-starred necklace she wore.
why: come Almeon a sua madre fé caro / parer lo sventurato addornamento; the line limped on a repeat.

old: long enough to see how lost your road has gone!
new: long enough to see the evil road you're on!
why: sì che veggiate il vostro mal sentiero.

old: voices were singing "Blessed are the poor in spirit" —
new: voices were singing "Beati pauperes spiritu" —
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XII.110 has the beatitude in Latin, as the edition does for every other terrace.

old: looking the part — and if you ask me how,
new: by the look of it — and if you ask me how,
why: un'ombra ch'aspettava / in vista: her look was one of waiting; 'looking the part' means seeming suitable.

old: said out loud, "They have no wine" —
new: said out loud, "Vinum non habent" —
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XIII.29 'Vinum non habent' is Latin.

old: now that your family has cleared out
new: now that your family is gone
why: poi che gita se n'è la tua famiglia; 'cleared out' is casual, near comic.

old: strikes you down."
new: strikes you."
why: onde vi batte chi tutto discerne: beats or chastises; 'down' suggests death. Closing line otherwise kept.

old: remained to the sun above us still to run.
new: was left for the sun above us to run.
why: essere al sol del suo corso rimaso; 'remained ... still' doubled.

old: You lie, though free, beneath a greater power
new: Though free, you are subject to a greater power
why: liberi soggiacete; aloud, 'You lie' lands as an accusation.

old: There is another good that brings no joy;
new: There is another good that does not make us happy;
why: Altro ben è che non fa l'uom felice: such goods please (hence 'too far' next) but do not bless.

old:
and a fanning across my face, and a voice:
"Beati pacifici — blessed are they
who are free of evil anger."
new:
and a fanning across my face, and a voice: "Beati
pacifici, who are free of evil anger!"
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XVII.68-69 'Beati / pacifici, che son sanz' ira mala!'; the English gloss 'blessed are they' removed, and the tercet is three lines again.

old:
either love of nature or love of the mind;
and this you know.
new: either of nature or of the mind; and this you know.
why: o naturale o d'animo; e tu 'l sai: one line in Dante; the stray fourth line rejoined.

old: its book of Ethics.
new: its moral teaching.
why: però moralità lasciaro al mondo: the title is read in by the edition.

old: Now, so that every other desire can be measured against this one,
new: Now, so that every other wish may fall in with this one,
why: perché a questa ogn' altra si raccoglia: gathered into accord, not measured.

old: "What is it with you, that
new: "What troubles you, that
why: Che hai che pur inver' la terra guati?; 'What is it with you' jars in Virgil's mouth.

old: the one for whom, above us, they still weep?
new: the one for whom alone, above us, they now weep?
why: che sola sovr' a noi omai si piagne: 'sola' and 'omai' were lost.

old: declaring that those who mourn are blessed,
new: declaring "Qui lugent" to be blessed,
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XIX.50 ''Qui lugent' affermando esser beati'.

old: "My soul has clung to the dust,"
new: "Adhaesit pavimento anima mea,"
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XIX.73 is the Latin psalm verse.

old: know this: that I was once the successor of Peter.
new: scias quod ego fui successor Petri.
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XIX.99 Adrian speaks this line in Latin.

old:
as the feeling that spurs our going moves us
now to a quicker, now to a slower pace.
new:
as the feeling that spurs us to speak
drives us now to a quicker, now a slower pace.
why: secondo l'affezion ch'a dir ci sprona: the pace is of speaking; these souls lie prone. Longfellow: 'desire of speech, that spurs us'.

old: "Glory to God in the highest" — that was what
new: "Gloria in excelsis Deo" — that was what
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): Dante XX.136 ''Gloria in excelsis' tutti 'Deo''.

old: a single gram.
new: a single dram.
why: non fermai peso di dramma; 'gram' is metric.

old: may he speed them up soon."
new: may he soon send them upward."
why: che tosto sù li 'nvii: send them up, not make them faster.

old:
'To what, O cursed hunger for gold,
do you not drive the appetites of men?'
new:
'Why, O holy hunger for gold,
do you not rule the appetites of men?'
why: Per che non reggi tu, o sacra fame / de l'oro, l'appetito de' mortali?: Statius reads Aeneid III.56-57 as a call to measure, which is what convicts him of prodigality. Longfellow follows Virgil instead.

old: and in what ditch."
new: and in what quarter."
why: in qual vico: a street or quarter; 'ditch' suggests the Malebolge.

old: the word "sitio"
new: the word "sitiunt"
why: Dante XXII.6 'con "sitiunt", sanz' altro': the beatitude's 'sitiunt' (they thirst), not 'sitio'. Found on verification; the reviewer's English rendering is rejected under Policy L.

old: and the smell of water — with no way to reach either?
new: and the smell of water — not knowing how?
why: e quel d'un'acqua, non sappiendo como: who would believe it, not knowing the cause; reaching the food is not said here.

old: and crying up toward the leaves I-don't-know-what,
new: and crying I don't know what up toward the leaves,
why: gridar non so che verso le fronde; the hyphenated compound reads oddly aloud.

old: So said a voice I-don't-know-whose among the boughs;
new: So said a voice among the boughs, I don't know whose;
why: non so chi, tra le frasche; same mannerism.

old: Our own offense was of both kinds at once;
new: Our own sin was between man and woman;
why: Nostro peccato fu ermafrodito: heterosexual, against the Sodomites; 'both kinds at once' suggests both sins.

old:
starting again, "who for a better life
take on a cargo of our borderlands.
new:
starting again, "who, so as to die better,
take on board the knowledge of our borderlands.
why: de le nostre marche ... per morir meglio, esperïenza imbarche: to die better; 'for a better life' follows Longfellow, not Dante.

old: was a better craftsman of the mother tongue.
new: was the better smith of the mother tongue.
why: il miglior fabbro del parlar materno: the known phrase.

old: Freely he began to speak — in his own tongue:
new: Freely he began to speak:
why: Policy L (Latin/Occitan stays in the original, no in-line English): El cominciò liberamente a dire: 'in his own tongue' is an in-line gloss announcing the Occitan.

old: stands only this wall."
new: stands this wall."
why: tra Bëatrice e te è questo muro: 'only' is added.

old:
though it moves under a dark, dark current
in a shade that never breaks —
new:
though it moves on dark, dark,
under a shade that never breaks —
why: si mova bruna bruna / sotto l'ombra perpetüa: the water itself is dark, under the shade.
Non che Roma di carro così bello / rallegrasse Affricano, o vero Augusto: 'not even Rome's' dangled.

old:
had not been brought to stand and shake before her,
had not stood trembling in her presence —
new:
had not been broken down with awe,
trembling in her presence —
why: ch'a la sua presenza / non era di stupor, tremando, affranto: one idea said twice; 'stupor' restored as awe.

old: among the living rafters of beams
new: among the living rafters
why: tra le vive travi: the rafters are the trees; 'of beams' muddles it.

old: that the voice moved, and yet went out
new: that the voice moved, and yet died
why: pria si spense: it died out; 'went out' first reads as 'came out'.

old: farther than she had outshone all others here.
new: farther than she outshone all others when she was on earth.
why: vincer che l'altre qui, quand' ella c'era: 'here' is earth; in Eden it pointed wrong.

old: Sure of itself as a fortress on a high peak,
new: Secure as a fortress on a high peak,
why: Sicura (feminine): the harlot is secure, not the chariot.

old: a wall of not-caring
new: a wall of indifference
why: di non caler parete; plain English has the word.

old:
made a shield, hiding from me the harlot
and the strange new beast.
new: made a shield between me and the harlot and the strange new beast.
why: Policy C (closing line): Dante XXXII.160 'a la puttana e a la nova belva' is one closing line; the segment had it broken over two.

old: the stone-stilling water of Elsa
new: the petrifying water of Elsa
why: acqua d'Elsa: its water coats things in stone; 'stone-stilling' is opaque.

old:
remade — the way new plants are renewed
with new leaves —
pure and ready
new:
remade, the way young plants are made new
when they put out new leaves,
pure and ready
why: Policy C (closing line): Dante XXXIII.142-145: the last tercet is three full lines again and the closing line 'puro e disposto a salire a le stelle' stands alone, unchanged, as the segment's last line (no 49th segment exists).
